title: Triodion: the Publican and the Pharisee to Holy Saturday
scope: One entry for every day from the Sunday of the Publican and the Pharisee (pascha -70) to Holy Saturday (pascha -1), keyed by days from Pascha.
licence: Released with bible-rs under the MIT licence. The table holds Scripture references only: no Bible text and no prose from the sources. Notes are our own.
usage: Antiochian Orthodox Christian Archdiocese of North America: Byzantine (Greek) usage, Revised Julian fixed feasts, Julian Paschalion. Slavic (OCA) and Greek (GOARCH) differences are kept in 'variants' and 'slavic' and never replace the main reading.
numbering: English Bible (KJV/Hebrew) chapter and verse, the grid's numbering, with half-verse letters dropped. Each string in refs is one contiguous range ('Book C:V', 'Book C:V-V' or 'Book C:V-C:V', with the grid's book abbreviations); a reading's refs are read together, in order, as one lesson.
confidence: high: an Antiochian-facing source agrees with at least one independent source. medium: the sources differ (usually by a verse at the start or end) or the reference rests on one source. low: no Antiochian or Greek source was found, or the yearly ordo decides.

sources.ANT-OLG: Antiochian Archdiocese, Department of Liturgics: Online Liturgical Guide service texts, 2023-2026 (antiochian.org/servicetexts). References only.
sources.ANT-CHART: Antiochian Archdiocese, Sunday Liturgical Readings Chart 2026 (antiochian.org/liturgicalinstructions).
sources.ANT: antiochian.org daily readings, 2018-2026 (the GOARCH Online Chapel feed, as harvested in orthocal-python's data/antiochian_raw).
sources.GOA: Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of America, Online Chapel daily readings, 2018-2030 (goarch.org; partly as harvested in orthocal-python).
sources.GOA-DCS: GOA Digital Chant Stand (dcs.goarch.org), 'Readings for the Day', 2026.
sources.OCA: Orthodox Church in America lectionary, via the orthocal.info API, 2010-2032. Slavic usage.
sources.HAP: Isabel F. Hapgood, Service Book of the Holy Orthodox-Catholic Apostolic (Greco-Russian) Church, 1906 (public domain; archive.org cu31924029363128): tables of Epistles and Gospels.
sources.SCR: F. H. Scrivener, A Plain Introduction to the Criticism of the New Testament, Cambridge 1861 (public domain; archive.org plainintroductio00scri): Synaxarion and Menologion of the Byzantine lectionary manuscripts.
sources.GRE: V. Grechulevich, Ukazatel tserkovnykh chtenii, St Petersburg 1853 (public domain): Slavic lectionary index with zachalo numbers.
sources.MCI: Metropolitan Cantor Institute (Byzantine Catholic Archeparchy of Pittsburgh), 'The Lectionary' (mci.archpitt.org). Slavic usage.
sources.NLM: New Liturgical Movement: descriptions of the Antiochian Paschal procession (2019) and the Royal Hours of Theophany (2017).
sources.WIKI: Wikipedia, articles on the Triodion and Holy Week (for Holy Week Old Testament readings only).

rules: Great Lent weekdays (pascha -48 to -9) have no Liturgy: Isaiah at the Sixth Hour, Genesis and Proverbs at Vespers (the Presanctified Liturgy on Wednesdays and Fridays). Cheesefare Wednesday and Friday are aliturgical too.
Readings are listed under the liturgical day they belong to; 'served' says when a service is held the evening before.
Sunday Matins Gospels from pascha -70 to -14 follow the eleven eothina (gospels.json).
Fixed feasts in this season (the Meeting, the Forty Martyrs, the Annunciation) are in menaion.json.

Saturday of Souls (Meatfare Saturday)
entries.note: First of the four Saturdays of Souls in this period (the next is the Saturday before Pentecost); kollyva and memorial service. Antiochian practice joins the departed Epistle to the day's Gospel.

entries.name: Sunday of the Last Judgment (Meatfare Sunday)
entries.note: Last day for meat. Matins Gospel follows the eothinon cycle (not listed).

entries.name: Monday of Cheesefare Week
entries.note: The Epistle is the whole of 3 John: 14 verses in KJV numbering (GOARCH prints 1:1-15 in RSV numbering, which splits v. 14).

entries.name: Thursday of Cheesefare Week
entries.note: Gospel verse selection differs by book: Greek feed 23:1-31, 33, 44-56; Slavic 23:2-34, 44-56; medieval Greek (SCR) 23:1-33, 44-56.

Forgiveness Sunday (Cheesefare Sunday)
entries.note: Expulsion of Adam from Paradise. Matins Gospel follows the eothinon cycle (not listed). Forgiveness Vespers that evening has no Old Testament readings. Great Lent begins.

entries.note: No Divine Liturgy. The Genesis and Proverbs readings belong to Vespers on the evening of this day. In the fifth week the Presanctified Liturgy moves from Wednesday to Thursday. The Great Canon of St Andrew is sung at Thursday's Matins, served on Wednesday evening.

entries.name: Thursday of the Great Canon (Fifth Week of Great Lent)
entries.note: Vespers is joined to the Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts. No Epistle or Gospel unless a Menaion feast or patronal feast is kept. Presanctified on Thursday this week, after the Great Canon; Antiochian instructions call it 'a consolation for the labor of the Great Canon'.

entries.name: Friday of the Fifth Week of Great Lent
entries.note: Vespers is joined to the Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts. No Epistle or Gospel unless a Menaion feast or patronal feast is kept. The Akathist Hymn is sung at Saturday's Matins, served on Friday evening.

entries.name: Saturday of the Akathist (Fifth Saturday of Great Lent)
entries.note: Liturgy of St John Chrysostom. The Akathist Hymn is sung at Matins (Friday evening). Antiochian sources disagree on the Gospel: the Archdiocese's own service text reads Luke 10:38-42, 11:27-28; its GOARCH-supplied readings feed shows Luke 1:39-49, 56.

entries.name: Sunday of St Mary of Egypt (Fifth Sunday of Great Lent)
entries.note: Liturgy of St Basil (the last Sunday on which it is served in Lent). Matins Gospel follows the eothinon cycle (not listed).

entries.name: Friday of the Sixth Week of Great Lent (eve of Lazarus Saturday)

readings.note: The Septuagint orders Proverbs 25-31 differently; this is the passage on the valiant woman, given in English numbering.

entries.note: Vespers is joined to the Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts. No Epistle or Gospel unless a Menaion feast or patronal feast is kept. Great Lent's forty days end at this Vespers, which begins Lazarus Saturday. Antiochian instructions place this Presanctified Liturgy in the morning or late afternoon.

entries.name: Lazarus Saturday
entries.note: Liturgy of St John Chrysostom with the baptismal hymn 'As many as have been baptized'. Matins has no Gospel. The Vespers readings of the evening before are under Pascha-9.

entries.name: Palm Sunday (Entry of the Lord into Jerusalem)
entries.note: Liturgy of St John Chrysostom. One of the Twelve Great Feasts. The Bridegroom Matins of Holy Monday, served this evening, is under Pascha-6.

entries.name: Great and Holy Monday
entries.note: Antiochian instructions place the Presanctified Liturgy in the morning. The custom of reading the four Gospels at the Little Hours on Monday to Wednesday has no fixed verse divisions and is not listed.

entries.name: Great and Holy Tuesday
Great and Holy Wednesday

readings.note: Only OCA checked for this reading.
The Septuagint adds at 2:22 the naming of Eliezer, which the Antiochian text (and English Bibles) give as Exod 18:4.

entries.note: Holy Unction is a sacramental service, not part of the Triodion cycle; Antiochian instructions direct parishes to serve it on Holy Wednesday evening. Holy Thursday Matins may also be served this night (listed under Pascha-3).

entries.name: Great and Holy Thursday

readings.note: End verse of the Job 38 portion varies: Antiochian 38:1-21, Hapgood 38:1-22, OCA 38:1-23.
optional rite after the Liturgy; reading before the washing

entries.note: Institution of the Mystical Supper. The Jeremiah prophecy is read at the First Hour on this day (not the Sixth). Antiochian instructions: Matins in the morning, followed by the Vesperal Liturgy; the Washing of the Feet may follow.

readings.title: 15th
readings.note: Septuagint Dan 3:1-88: Daniel 3:1-23, then the Prayer of Azariah and the Song of the Three Youths through 'Bless the Lord, Ananias, Azarias and Misael'. Sung with the refrain 'Praise the Lord and supremely exalt Him'.

entries.note: Matins with the Lamentations at the tomb is served on Friday evening. The Vesperal Liturgy is the first Liturgy of Pascha, with baptisms. Antiochian rubric: at least readings 1-6 and 15 are read; its shorter parish text reads only Genesis, Jonah and Daniel. 'Arise, O God' replaces the Alleluia before the Gospel.
